subject: Quarantine-slice plan: pinning windows and rollback runway for AcmeHealth Private
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>, Alice Turner <ops@acmehealth.com>

Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quarantine-slice plan: pinning windows and rollback runway for AcmeHealth Private

Hi all,

Summary / goal: coordinate a low-risk maintenance window to apply a minor runtime patch to AcmeHealth's private cluster, using a quarantine "slice" approach so we can pin a subset of hosts, validate telemetry, and roll back cleanly if needed. This thread is to lock the window, owners, and the rollback runway.

Key proposal (high level):
- Create a quarantine slice (10% of capacity) in the customer's private VPC and pin it to runtime version 2027.04.1 (pin TTL = 72h).
- Route a small fraction of traffic to the slice for a 2-hour canary. Network level quarantine uses AWS VPC Network ACL rules + BGP community tag to keep traffic isolated from other tenants.
- Preflight checks: snapshot KV cache, export live traces, run synthetic prompts and evaluate latency/regression tests.
- Rollback runway: immediate revert to 2027.03.x via automated snapshot restore (target RTO for revert: 15 minutes from decision).

Ask: approve maintenance window options and owners below, and confirm Acme ops contacts for playcall.

Windows (PDT):
- Option A: Mon 2027-04-26 01:00-03:00 (preferred, narrow customer traffic)
- Option B: Tue 2027-04-27 22:00-00:00 (backup)

Owners / roles:
- Release lead: maya_srinivasan (Redwood)
- Network fence: karthik_iyer (Redwood)
- Safety/rollback: rishi_malhotra (Redwood)
- Customer liaison / billing: Jorge Ramos (Acme) / monica_patel (Redwood)
- Compliance / approval: neha_kapoor (Redwood)

Attachments: quarantine-slice-matrix.xlsx (traffic split and canary thresholds), netflow-diagram.svg (quarantine network path), rollback-checklist.pdf (rollback steps, verification criteria).

Notes / constraints:
- We'll avoid any global DNS changes; traffic split will be handled by the routing layer and VPC ACLs to make the slice invisible to other services.
- We expect degraded tail latency on the slice for up to 10 minutes during warm-up. No data-migration required.

Next steps: please reply with your preferred window (A/B), any objections to the network fencing approach, and confirm the on-call numbers to include on the playcall.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Staff PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Apr 23, 2027 at 09:12 AM Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com> wrote:
> Summary / goal: coordinate a low-risk maintenance window ...

Quick technical notes from my side:
- Network fencing: prefer BGP community tagging at the edge + VPC route table isolation. NACLs are fine as a second layer but can be noisy for ephemeral tests. We'll program the quarantine community on the eBGP peer with Acme's edge.
- IP plan: quarantine slice will use a dedicated /26 drawn from customer allocation (see netflow-diagram.svg).
- Drains: we'll stagger pod drains by zone (max 20% per zone) and use the runtime's KV-snapshot API (snapshot id pattern: acme-20270423-sliceX) before any config change.
- Canary checks (automated): 50 synthetic prompts, correctness threshold >= 98% pass, latency p95 < baseline + 120ms. Failure triggers immediate rollback.
- Rollback automation: the script is under release/tools/revert_slice.sh (safe mode) — it restores pinned version, reconverges routes, and replays KV snapshot application. I recommend an explicit 15-minute "decision window" post-canary before expanding.

Risks: if eBGP manipulation fails, we fall back to contract-level routing (health-proxy override) which is slower but safe. Need Acme edge engineer on the bridge for the first 10 minutes.

I approve Option A provided Acme confirms edge availability.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quarantine-slice plan: pinning windows and rollback runway for AcmeHealth Private

Thanks Maya — I reviewed the plan. A few compliance gating items before we give greenlight: 

1) Audit/log retention: we need to ensure the canary slice is forwarding full request traces and audit logs to Acme's centralized S3 bucket/ SIEM for the 72h pinning period. Please confirm the bucket ARN and ACLs.
2) Data handling: confirm there are no new PII flows; we must not enable any debug dumps that include raw user prompts.
3) Change approval: we require a signed change form (DocuSign or equivalent) for the Option A window. If Acme prefers, we can attach the change form to this thread — I've prepared a template in the drive link.
4) Post-change evidence: within 2 hours of completion, provide exported traces and the canary evaluation report. This will be appended to Acme's compliance folder.

I've attached rollback-checklist.pdf with the minimal verification gates we will use to mark the rollback decision. Please confirm Acme's security contact for the playcall so we can include them in the audit timeline.

If all of the above are OK, I'm comfortable with the 72h pin TTL and the 15-minute decision window.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Compliance, Redwood Inference
